Now we soon plan to raise another INR150 crores in H1°25 to fund our FY 25 extension plan, and process for the same is initiated

items.statement: APL Apollo subscribed to warrants and holds 37% of turnover; no further shareholding changes expected
items.quote: They have subscribed to the warrants. I think that's going on. There shouldn't be any change in the shareholding, no changes expected.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances increased to INR34 crores from INR12 crores in previous year
items.quote: Our cash and bank balances for the year stood at INR34 crores compare to INR12 crores in the last year.

items.statement: Working capital maintained at around 30 days with inventory 30 days, debtors 40 days, creditors 40 days
items.quote: For t he second part for the inventory will be approximately around 30 the days. Debtors approximately 40 days, and creditors will be around 40 days. So net average will be around 30 days

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 150 days in FY24 from 159 days in FY23, driven by reduction in inventory days from 108 to 97 days.
items.quote: The cash conversion cycle in FY24 improved to 150 days down from 159 days in FY23. Largely attributed to reduction in inventory days, this reduction in inventory days can be primarily attributed to the removal of high-value inventory from the system.

items.statement: Receivables excluding Himachal Pradesh at 68 days; HP receivables increased significantly due to election-related delays, similar to FY19 when days reached ~98; payments from HP started in April-May
items.quote: During this quarter, our receivables stand out to be 68 days excluding receivable from Himachal Pradesh. We experienced a significant increase in receivable from HP, leading to higher working capital costs.

items.statement: Working capital stretched due to increased receivables; finance costs expected to reduce as receivables stabilize by end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: We see our working capital currently at stretch due to increase in receivables . it will be getting stabilized by end of Q1. we would see reduction in the finance cost.

items.statement: HP receivables recovery expected between June and August 2024 after elections conclude; full smoothening by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: I believe it will take until the end of Q2 because the elections we get over in June and from there on, then the process will reinitiate again. So we believe between June, July, August, we should be able to recover our receivables.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations to EBITDA was above 90% target for FY24, one of the highest in the industry
items.quote: Moreover, due to our neighborhood model, approximately 90% of our patient business is from cash and insurance patients only, which has enabled us to achieve cash flow from operations through EBITDA above our target of being 90% for the year, one of the highest in the industry, which reaffirms our model.

items.statement: Working capital requirement for biodiesel plant estimated at INR15-20 crores based on 21-25 days OMC receivables
items.quote: Working capital around INR15 crores, INR 20 crores whatever will be the outstanding towards the OMCs

items.statement: Management expects existing inventory to reduce 40-45% over next two years and aims to bring down overall debt by about Rs 100 crore over the same period, demonstrating free cash flow generation.
items.value: 40% to 45% inventory reduction; Rs 100 crore debt reduction
items.quote: We expect the existing inventory to be reduced by around 40% to 45% in the next two years, this is not considering fresh investments in content. Furthermo re, we are also aiming to bring down the overall debt by about 100 crore over the next two

items.statement: Investment in new initiatives for FY25 estimated at approximately Rs 50 crore, significantly lower than Rs 81 crore spent in FY24.
items.quote: We are estimating that investme nt to be approximately in the range of about 50 crores

items.statement: Incremental inventory write-off due to policy change was approximately Rs 10 crore in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: Approximately around 10 odd crore incremental write off would be there.

items.statement: Two new Independent Directors have been appointed and details filed with exchanges on Friday.
items.quote: Yes, two new Independent Direc tors have already been appointed. Management: See the outcome of the meeting it clearly states the appointment details. Hiren Gada: Yes, this was filed on Friday i tself, the details of the two Independent Directors

items.statement: Consolidated cash and cash equivalents were INR 202 crores as of 31 March 2024
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 202 crores on a consolidated basis as of 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Dehradun community cash surplus of INR 125 crores as of March 2024
items.quote: The operational revenue for the Dehradun community increased to INR22 crores in FY 24, a growth of 32% over last year. And due to robust sales, the community continues to be PBT and cash positive with a cash surplus of INR 125 crores as of March '24.

items.statement: Treasury and monetizable assets at INR 435 crores as of March 2024
items.quote: Our treasury and other monetizable assets stood at a very healthy number of INR 435 crores as of March '24, so very strong balance sheet and a consolidated net worth of INR 492 crores as of March end.

items.statement: No capital raise currently planned but possible with future scale-up
items.quote: Not as yet. We could be, but not as yet. We are well funded now, but maybe when we see scale up and growth coming through, then yes, we could be. But we can't confirm them as yet.

items.statement: Raymond Simkins, a director and ~11% shareholder, is joining as co-promoter via a shareholders agreement that triggered an open offer currently underway.
items.quote: One of my co-directors on the Board, Mr. Raymond Simkins, who has also been a sha reholder holding over about 11% shares for almost over a decade or more, had a d esire to join me as a co- promoter since the reclassification of the ex-promoter

items.statement: Open offer expected to open first week of June and close by third week of June, pending SEBI approval.
items.quote: I think the offer dates, we are just awaiting the SEBI approval. But it's expected to open up in the first week of June and by the third week of June, it should end.

items.statement: Open offer price set at Rs. 147 based on SEBI formula (Rs. 146 odd), slightly above the regulated price.
items.quote: And it's slightly incorrect, the date was announced, just prior to that the price s were lower. And it's only after the announcement that it came up, but the SEBI form ula rate came to Rs. 146 and some odd amount. And it's always advisable to do a round figure. So, in fact, we are slightly higher than the SEBI formula

items.statement: Warrant issue from November 2022 has an 18-month period ending June 2024; investors' equity money expected by June end.
items.quote: We have that warrant issue, which actually happened in Novemb er of ‘22 for which the 18-month period actually ends in June of 2024. So, having said t hat, unless we grow our sales drastically, we might not need more amount of working capital debt

items.statement: Operating cash flow generation expected to be positive in FY25 with cash breakeven in API subsidiary
items.quote: There may be cash breakeven. Yes, we are anticipating cash breakeven there.

items.statement: ESOP pool of up to 5% of paid-up capital approved for API subsidiary
items.quote: We have in the API, got an approval from the shareholders and the investors up to 5% of the total paid up capital.

items.statement: Free cash flow of INR7-8 crores available due to reduced inventory and better debtor control
items.quote: We have, I mean, free cash flows available to the tune of INR7 crores to INR8 crores. That is possible because we have reduced the inventory and als o got better debtor control as compared to the previous year

items.statement: Net debt rose to Rs 86 Crores due to new real estate JVs and EPC bid commitments
items.quote: As a result, our net debt has risen to Rs 86 Crores.

items.statement: QIP planned in next few months for Santa Cruz project funding
items.quote: we had gone ahead with the QIP requirement in the market which currently is very much in line and we should be hopefully doing it in the next few months.

items.statement: Cash reserve stood at INR327 crores as of 31st March 2024 with strong liquidity position
items.quote: Our cash reserve stood at INR327 crores as of 31st March 2024. Our liquidity position remains strong.

items.statement: Highest ever operating cash flows of Rs1,211m in FY24 vs Rs811m in FY23
items.quote: Our greatest achievement during FY24 has been the commendable work done in improving the working capital metrics which resulted in the highest operating cash flows in the company's history at Rs1,211m vs Rs811 last year.

items.statement: Free cash flow positive in FY24
items.quote: We continued to be Free Cash Flow positive as well.

items.statement: Trade receivables reduced to Rs2,601m in Q4 FY24 from Rs2,653m in Q4 FY23 despite higher sales
items.quote: Trade Receivables reduced to Rs2,601m during Q4FY24 vs Rs2,653m during Q4FY23. This is a Rs52m decrease in receivables in spite of achieving incremental sales of Rs523m over last year.

items.statement: Receivable days improved to 143 days in Q4 FY24 from 159 days in Q4 FY23
items.quote: In terms of receivable days, it stood at 143 days (vs. 159 days in Q4FY23), a reduction of 16 days during FY24. This is the lowest Q4 receivable days in the company's history.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced to 157 days in Q4 FY24 from 188 days in Q4 FY23
items.quote: Net Working Capital reduced to 157 days (vs. 188 days in Q4FY23) which is a reduction of 31 days during FY24. This is the lowest Q4 net working capital days in the company's history.

items.statement: Net cash balance of Rs600m at end of FY24 vs net debt of Rs60m at end of FY23
items.quote: We were Net Cash positive as of March 2024 at Rs. 600 Mn vs Net Debt of 60m at the same time last year.

items.statement: Targeting to be net debt free for 3 quarters in FY25
items.quote: We are targeting to be Net Debt Free for 3 quarters during the year.

items.statement: Buyback consideration once cash crosses Rs100cr
items.quote: Once we hit let's say 100cr. plus in terms of cash, then we will probably start thinking of buyback.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was Rs 46 crore in FY24, higher than the previous year, indicating efficient working capital management.
items.quote: I would like to add that our cash flow from operations is 46 crores during the current year, which is more than the previous year . This indicates level of high e fficiency in working capital management

items.statement: Cash from operations expected to turn positive by Q3 FY25 as new product lines start generating revenue
items.quote: So maybe by quarter 3 of this year. A lot of money that is right now being invested into the new product lines, the new talent that we are hiring, setting up of the new lines for these products, which we briefly mentioned.

items.statement: DSO increased to 46 days from 33 days last year due to increased billing in Q4
items.quote: The DSO was at 46 days as compared to 33 days last year, but that was also because of increased billing and business that we had in quarter 4.

items.statement: Net cash at end of quarter was INR7,185 million, up marginally from INR7,179 million last quarter and INR7,157 million last year
items.quote: Net cash at the end of the quarter was INR7,185 million, and this is a small increase over INR7,179 million last quarter and INR7,157 million last year.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR0.75 per share in addition to interim dividend of INR0.50 per share paid in October 2023
items.quote: Based on the results, the Board of Directors met today and recommended a dividend of INR0.75 per share, final dividend of INR0.75 per share versus or this was in addition to the interim dividend of INR0.50 per share, which was paid in October 31 -- on October 31, 2023.

items.statement: Promoter stake increased in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Also a point which was missed in my earlier discussion and also in the presentation is that promoter stake has also increased in the fourth quarter of FY24, which will also be something which is appreciated by all shareholders.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 43.9 crore equity infusion via preferential allotment of shares and warrants; Rs 28.9 crore received by end-March against shares and 25% of warrants.
items.quote: In the 4 th quarter the board of directors approved the infusion of Rs. 43.9 crores of equity by way of preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants. Of this Rs. 28.9 crores approximately was received at the end of March against the preferential allotment of equity shares and 25% of the warrants that were issued.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt increased by INR 193 crores to INR 407 crores as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: On the 31st March, 2024 the net debt at the consolidated level stood at INR 407 crores, an increase of INR 193 crores as compared to the last quarter.

items.statement: Finance cost increased due to higher inventory and higher interest rates; lease accounting added ~Rs 4 crore to finance cost.
items.quote: And as far as finance cost is concerned, yes because there was higher inventory in the system as compared to last year and also the interest rates have gone up as compared to last two years. So that is also actually the interest cost have gone up because of these two reasons.

items.statement: Finance cost expected to come down 100-200 basis points in FY25 as old stock is liquidated.
items.quote: The finance cost will come down in this financial year as we are liquidating some old stock also. So one thing | am pretty sure about that, it should be coming down to 100 to 200 basis points

items.statement: Sudarshan Farm Chemicals acquisition involved a common board member, making it a related-party transaction
items.quote: the acquisition of Sudarshan Farm Chemicals, the Rs. 30 crores turnover company for which you paid almost Rs. 130 crores and there is a common board member on your company and this company, so in a way there is some related party reference

items.statement: Net cash flow from operations grew from Rs.36 crores in FY22 to Rs.112 crores in FY24
items.quote: Also , there is a healthy growth in the net cash flow from operations from Rs.36 crores in FY'22 to Rs.112 close in FY'24.

items.statement: Management says no dilution is planned in the next 12 months but will update when expansion plans are finalized.
items.quote: Sir, nothing planned right now. We have too many things. It is too early for me to state anything. But there are too many things going on in our mind with their expansions and we will definitely be coming back to you the way we plan.

items.statement: Restructuring of HEG and Bhilwara Energy led to fair valuation and unrealized mark-to-market gain of ₹138 crore for RSWM's 7.56% stake
items.quote: You are right that the restructuring of HEG and Bhilwara Energy has led to this fair evaluation and it resulted into the fair valuation mark to market gains to RSWM also since it has around 7.56% shareholding in this.

items.statement: Two new directors added to the board: Mr. Haren Parekh as independent director and Mr. Kuldeep Tiwari as Executive Director for operations.
items.quote: On other issues you can see that we've added a couple of directors at our recent board meeting. One of them is Mr. Haren Parekh, who's a seasoned finance professional. He was CFO of HDB Financial Services and he comes with almost 3 decades of experience. We also added another person, Mr. Kuldeep Tiwari, as an Executive Director to head our operations and he brings with him a couple of decades of o

items.statement: Management plans to raise equity this fiscal to strengthen the balance sheet and deleverage.
items.quote: So keeping all of these things in line, we would like to strengthen and raise equity sometime this fiscal, that's what we're running for.

items.statement: Management says no immediate fundraising; may consider raising capital for credit business later after proving model with own capital.
items.quote: Directionally, there might be need to think about fundraising for the credit business, but something that we are going to come back on. I think right now our focus is to make sure that we drive operating leverage and make sure that many things especially on the credit side, we're able to build products that wor th using our own c apital, maybe work in a some sort of a co-lending model, but initial

items.statement: Cash generated from operations was INR156 crores in FY24, used to reduce net debt to INR6 crores from INR134 crores a year earlier.
items.quote: Cash generated from operations stands at INR156 crores positive which is mainly utilised in reducing our net debt. Our net debt has reduced significantly as on March 24 and stands at INR6 crores versus INR134 crores last year.

items.statement: Received INR 30 crores of outstanding tax refunds in Q4 FY24
items.quote: In the last quarter, we received almost INR 30 crores of this amount.

items.statement: Working capital stabilized over past 5-6 quarters post-COVID, reducing incremental requirements
items.quote: Over the past 5-6 quarters, as our business has stabilized post-COVID, we've reached a point where incremental working capital requirements have not significantly increased.

items.statement: Consciously controlled CapEx in FY23 to observe industry performance, improving cash flow
items.quote: Additionally, last year, we consciously controlled our capital expenditures (CapEx) to observe industry performance.

items.statement: Operating cash flow lower due to higher working capital from inventory and debtor build-up for targeted 15% growth
items.quote: So, operating cash flow is on the lower side, because of increase of working capital requirements. So, as you can see that, we have increase in inventory and debtors also and this represents mostly, the target this is the end of the year, and we are targeting minimum growth of 15%.

items.statement: Company generated Rs. 47 crore cash flow in FY24 while PAT was Rs. 30 crore
items.quote: My EBITDA is at 9% to 10%, and after accounting for depreciation and other line items, PAT came to Rs. 30 crore. However, the company has generated a cash flow of Rs. 47 crore.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was negative in FY24 because the company reduced creditors by about INR170 crores to improve the balance sheet and gain cash discounts.
items.quote: The main objective, as we have explained during our IPO process also, is that we would want to reduce our payable days. We want to gain on the cash discounts by negotiating better in the markets and all that. So during the current year, the focus has been to improve the balance sheet by reducing liabilities, etc.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs 300 crore with Rs 175 crore fresh issue and Rs 125 crore OFS
items.quote: Krystal, through this listing, we raised Rs. 300 crores, about 125 was OFS and 175 was our fresh issue.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 175 crore fresh issue allocated to working capital, capex, debt repayment and general corporate purposes
items.quote: Out of 175 also, we had the objects which were very clear, some small repayment of borrowings, funding towards working capital requirement, CAPEX and towards new machinery and general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Government and corporate receivable days are about 70 to 75 days
items.quote: Again, receivable days, generally also if you have both government and corporate they are about 70 to 75 days.
